messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] logical limits on variables
parts:
On 8/17/12 1:50 AM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> I was amused to come across this:
> http://andrewgelman.com/2008/05/axes_that_exten/
> which anticipates some of what we're doing with upper and lower bounds in Stan.

That's eerily prescient, right down to the defaults for matrices:

What I think would be better is for every data object to have
a ï¿½typeï¿½ attached: the type could be integer, nonnegative integer,
positive integer, continuous, nonnegative continuous, binary, discrete
with bounded range, discrete with specified labels, unordered discrete,
continuous between 0 and 1, etc. If the type is not specified (i.e., NULL),
it could default to unconstrained continuous

One thing we don't have is named categorical
outcomes. Everything is just integers.

I'm a big believer in strong type systems. Both of my
books have "type" in the title.

I'm just tidying up the named bounds and then I'll push
through changes to the models, web docs, and manual.

I didn't add upper/lower bounds for matrices or integer
matrices yet, but both are doable with some work.

- Bob
